Definition: to be untrue, in word (to lie, feign, disown) or deed (to disappoint, fail, cringe)
BiblicalUsage: Kachash is to be untrue — to lie, to feign, to deny, to disappoint. Sarah denied that she laughed; the law forbids lying to one another; the proverb prays not to be fed with lies; and Joshua sets up a stone that will witness against Israel if they deny their God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe lying is never small, because it strikes at the God who is truth itself. Every denial, every feigned word, is a little rehearsal of unbelief — and I would rather be caught telling an uncomfortable truth than a comfortable lie.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
